proj_card_fisformer_desc: An innovative architecture that replaces the conventional self-attention mechanism in Transformers with a Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) to model uncertainty and improve interpretability.
proj_fisformer_title: FISformer: Replacing Self-Attention with a Fuzzy Inference System in Transformer Models for Time Series Forecasting
proj_fisformer_abstract: Transformers have achieved remarkable progress in time series forecasting, yet their reliance on deterministic dot-product attention limits their capacity to model uncertainty and nonlinear dependencies across multivariate temporal dimensions. To address this limitation, we propose FISformer, a Fuzzy Inference System-Driven Transformer that replaces conventional attention with a FIS Interaction mechanism. In this framework, each query-key pair undergoes a fuzzy inference process for every feature dimension, where learnable membership functions and rule-based reasoning estimate token-wise relational strengths. These FIS-derived interaction weights capture uncertainty and provide interpretable, continuous mappings between tokens. A softmax operation is applied along the token axis to normalize these weights, which are then combined with the corresponding value features through element-wise multiplication to yield the final context-enhanced token representations. This design fuses the interpretability and uncertainty modeling of fuzzy logic with the representational power of Transformers. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that FISformer achieves superior forecasting accuracy, noise robustness, and interpretability compared to state-of-the-art Transformer variants, establishing fuzzy inference as an effective alternative to conventional attention mechanisms.
proj_fisformer_method_desc: Instead of conventional dot-product similarity, FISformer embeds a complete first-order Sugeno Fuzzy Inference System into the query-key interaction. This operates in four key stages:
proj_fisformer_method_1: Fuzzification: Query and key embeddings are mapped to fuzzy membership degrees using learnable Gaussian membership functions.
proj_fisformer_method_2: Rule Generation: Fuzzy rules are formulated using a product-based t-norm to compute the firing strength of each rule.
proj_fisformer_method_3: Defuzzification: The activations of all rules are normalized and aggregated to produce a defuzzified Fuzzy Interaction Map.
proj_fisformer_method_4: FIS Interaction: A softmax operation normalizes these weights, which are then combined with value features through element-wise multiplication.

proj_acc_abstract: The system being built is not a static tool serving a single institution (e.g., MÜDEK); it is a configurable accreditation framework engine. All authorized bodies under YÖKAK (such as MÜDEK, HEPDAK, FEDEK, KİDR) share the same Outcome-Based Education (OBE) backbone. The system manages varying criteria sets and report templates not with hardcoded software updates, but through data-based "framework packages" loaded into the engine.
proj_acc_arch_desc: The system consists of two main layers: an immutable core and a highly flexible configuration layer:
proj_acc_arch_core: Immutable Core: The Outcome-Based Education (OBE) backbone, multi-tenancy infrastructure, auditable evidence pool, and dynamic Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
proj_acc_arch_pkg: Mutable Layer (Framework Packages): Institution-specific criteria trees, outcome sets, report templates, mapping matrices, and specialized extension points.
proj_acc_mod_1: Program definition (PEOs, POs) and flexible institutional outcome mapping.
proj_acc_mod_2: Curriculum and course catalog management fully integrated with existing Student Information Systems (OBS) and the Bologna process.
proj_acc_mod_3: A transparent assessment and evaluation engine utilizing rubrics, question-based outcome analysis, and deterministic calculation rules.
proj_acc_mod_4: A polymorphic, version-controlled central evidence pool that provides complete audit trails and can be attached to any data entity.
proj_acc_mod_5: Artificial Intelligence (AI) driven sentiment and thematic analysis of open-ended responses from student, alumni, and employer surveys.
proj_acc_mod_6: Assignment and step-by-step tracking of PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) actions addressing identified deficiencies.
proj_acc_mod_7: An automated Self-Assessment Report (ÖDR) generator that is strictly compliant with the selected accreditation body's (e.g., MÜDEK) current standards and fully supported by linked evidence.
proj_acc_ai_desc: In this system, AI never writes directly to the system of record; grades, measurement numbers, and evidence remain completely deterministic (rule-based). AI acts solely as an "assistant" for tasks such as semi-automatic mapping of exam questions to outcomes, drafting ÖDR text, gap analysis, and evaluating open-ended surveys. The system ensures strict data isolation (tenant-isolated RAG) between universities; one institution's data is never used to train models for another.
proj_acc_tech_desc: The platform is built on a modern, .NET-based modular monolith architecture. It utilizes PostgreSQL for relational data management and advanced vector databases for AI context retrieval (RAG). For the MVP (Minimum Viable Product) phase, the MÜDEK Version 3.0 framework is being deployed, using the Gaziantep University Computer Engineering department as the primary reference.
